content: 1. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of fosphenytoin by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Conversely, fosphenytoin decreases voriconazole levels by enhancing its metabolism. Close monitoring is required when these drugs are co-administered. 2. Fosphenytoin reduces voriconazole levels or effects by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is significant, and alternative therapies should be considered. 3. Voriconazole increases fostamatinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate exposure to R406, the active metabolite of fostamatinib, necessitating close monitoring for toxicities and potential dose adjustments. 4. Both voriconazole and fostemsavir prolong the QTc interval. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 5. Co-administration of gadobenate and voriconazole is contraindicated as both drugs increase the QTc interval, posing a significant risk. 6. Voriconazole may increase gefitinib levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors can elevate the risk of gefitinib-related adverse effects, requiring close monitoring. 7. Voriconazole and gemifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are necessary when these drugs are used together. 8. Voriconazole decreases gentamicin levels through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain. 9. Voriconazole increases giltritinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative therapies used. If unavoidable, monitor for giltritinib-related adverse effects. 10. Voriconazole and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. If co-administration cannot be avoided, obtain ECGs at baseline, during treatment, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or increases by more than 60 ms from baseline. 11. Voriconazole increases glasdegib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. If unavoidable, monitor for QTc prolongation risks. 12. Voriconazole increases glimepiride levels by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are required. 13. Voriconazole increases glyburide levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Strong CYP2C9 inhibitors may further decrease glyburide metabolism. Close monitoring is necessary. 14. Voriconazole increases the toxicity of goserelin by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 15. Voriconazole increases guanfacine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly elevate guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dose to half the recommended amount. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are unavailable. 16. Voriconazole increases haloperidol levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 17. Voriconazole increases hydrocodone levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Close monitoring is essential. 18. Voriconazole increases hydrocortisone levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 19. Voriconazole and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative therapies used. 20. Voriconazole increases ibrutinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. When co-administered with voriconazole 200 mg twice daily, reduce the ibrutinib dose to 140 mg daily for B-cell malignancies or 280 mg daily for graft-versus-host disease. Resume the previous ibrutinib dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 21. Voriconazole increases ibuprofen levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain. 22. Voriconazole and ibutilide both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative therapies used. 23. Voriconazole increases idelalisib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative therapies used. If unavoidable, monitor for idelalisib toxicity and adjust the dosage as needed. 24. Voriconazole decreases ifosfamide levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active alkylating metabolites, decreasing its efficacy. Close monitoring is required. 25. Voriconazole increases iloperidone levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 26. Voriconazole increases imipramine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain. 27. Voriconazole increases lansoprazole levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain. 28. Voriconazole increases lapatinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 29. Voriconazole increases larotrectinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative therapies used.
